changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For event-driven buyers with scheduled peaks (such as ticket on-sales), and especially their operations leaders: lead with who, not tiers. Draft: 'A name, not a queue: someone who picks up on your on-sale morning.' Introduce the named people on the account and the coverage planned for each peak. Do not walk through plan tiers or response-time timers. Use only once the named coverage can actually be committed.
changes.why: The decider dismissed our tiered support as 'a queue with a faster timer' and asked 'who's my person', and the rep reports that 'Nobody said 'support.' They said 'who.''

changes.change: For operations decision-makers buying after a public payment failure: lead with incident response before uptime, capacity or developer claims. Use the customer's line as the frame: 'I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down.' Follow with what happens in the first minutes of a failure and who responds.
changes.why: The trigger was a support reply that came after the on-sale was over, and the decider gave our load-test results only 'good', so the technical story did not answer her question.

changes.change: New proof asset for peak-event buyers: a written, customizable 'on-sale morning' plan showing who is watching, who the customer calls, and what happens if payments start failing minutes in. Offer it to the operations decider before she asks. This is an internal action first, because the rep says 'We don't have that as a thing.'
changes.why: The decider wanted to see 'on paper, what we do on an on-sale morning', and the rep says we had no such plan and he did not build one with the solutions engineer.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For peak-event operations buyers: replace logo proof with a person. Offer a reference from a comparable customer who can describe a live incident and who picked up. Pair it with an introduction to our own named account team.
changes.why: The rep says 'I had logos. I didn't have a person.' The competitor brought the people who would be on the account, and the criteria shifted from throughput to 'names'.
